questions.question: Show the full log entries for signature log:payment.provider_timeout around minute 30.
Provide the time‑series data for metric:payment:error_rate:30 and its latency metrics at minute 30.
List any deploys or flag changes (e.g., flag:checkout-v2) applied before minute 30.

findings.text: Full log entries for signature log:payment.provider_timeout around minute 30 show repeated timeouts from provider acme-pay, e.g., "payment: provider acme-pay timed out after 3000 ms" at minute 30.
payment error_rate at minute 30 is not recorded; the next minute (31) jumps to 0.1344, about 34× the baseline 0.004
payment latency_p95 at minute 30 is missing; at minute 31 it spikes to 4979 ms, roughly 10× the baseline 479.267 ms
No deploys were recorded before minute 30.
No flag changes occurred before minute 30; all flags retain their default values.

hypotheses.summary: External payment provider acme‑pay timed out, causing payment error_rate and latency spikes that cascade to cart and web.
Payment service saturation more than doubled, leading to request queueing and timeouts.
Cart worker pool exhausted as it waited on slow payment responses, increasing error_rate and latency.
Web error_rate rose after downstream failures, but no direct fault observed in web itself.

data.rationale: Enabling the fallback flag routes payments away from the timed‑out acme‑pay provider, removing the slow external dependency.

prose.summary: At minute 30 a slow_payment fault was injected into the payment service, causing latency spikes. An alert fired at minute 32, prompting investigation at minute 34. The top hypothesis identified the payment provider slowdown. At minute 60 a fallback was proposed, approved, and applied, restoring the SLO by minute 66.
prose.rootCause: Injected slow_payment fault in the payment service caused provider latency, leading to SLO breach.
prose.whatWentWell: Alert triggered quickly, investigation started promptly, hypothesis ranking correctly identified payment as the issue, and the fallback proposal was approved and applied within minutes, restoring service health.
actionItems: Add automated detection for payment latency spikes.
Implement auto‑enable of payment-provider fallback on high latency.
Review and tighten fault injection testing procedures.
Adjust alert thresholds to reduce detection latency.
